summary: James W. Benson is an indologist and linguist. He served as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1974–1978) and served as a research fellow and director (1991–2001) at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

Linguist James Wilson Bright studied at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1885) and Johns Hopkins University (~1882–1924).
Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thayé (1813–1899) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Thekchok Dorje and as a pupil of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1840–1892).

Jamie Hubbard is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Kazuo Okabe and Minoru Kiyota, later serving as a professor at Smith College (attested 2016).

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1973–1979) and worked as a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1979–2004, attested 2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (attested 1995) and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.
Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Director (attested 1991) and Professor (attested 2015) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampa Tegchok (1930–2014) studied at Sera Monastery in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1982), Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993), and Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Jan C. Heesterman (1925–2014) was an Indology scholar who held a post at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990, where he is attested as Professor in 2014.
Jan Chozen Bays works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada (attested 2011), and became abbess at Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Jan Gonda was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Utrecht University (PhD 1929) and Leiden University. He held a chair at Utrecht University (1932–1950) and a post at the University of Chicago.

Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) specialized in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1923–1927) under Stanisław Schayer and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1927–1930).
Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1907–1911). He spent his academic career there, holding posts in 1919 and from 1930 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (~1962–1969) and the University of Bristol (~1970–1979) in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1978–1990) and the University of Groningen (~1990–2009).

Jan Nattier studied at Indiana and Harvard universities in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She held professorships at Macalester College, University of Hawaii, Indiana University, Soka University, and Stanford University.

Jan P. Hogendijk is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Utrecht University (~1974–1983). He held posts at Brown University (~1985–1986), Utrecht University (~1986), and Leiden University (~2004–2009).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper. He also studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.
